name: k-Means Clustering
description: k-Means is an unsupervised learning algorithm that partitions n observations into k clusters where each observation belongs to the cluster with the nearest mean (centroid). It minimizes the within-cluster sum of squares (variance).
how_it_works: The algorithm iteratively assigns data points to the nearest centroid based on Euclidean distance, then recalculates centroids as the mean of assigned points. This process repeats until centroids stabilize or maximum iterations reached. It converges to a local minimum of the within-cluster sum of squares.

complexity.time: O(n * k * d * i) where n=points, k=clusters, d=dimensions, i=iterations
complexity.space: O(n * d + k * d) for storing points and centroids

key_parameters: k: number of clusters to form
tolerance: convergence threshold for centroid movement
n_init: number of times to run with different seeds
pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Initialize k centroids randomly. Repeat: assign each point to nearest centroid (clustering step), recompute centroids as mean of assigned points (update step). Continue until centroids move less than tolerance or max_iterations reached. k-means++ initialization improves results by spreading initial centroids.
